claim_scope: Asset Transfer Core V1 is a bounded deterministic ordinary-transfer functional core whose shared no_std arithmetic derives exact debit and credit balances, whose typed leaf derives canonical post-state and one global account-movement row, and whose rejected shape carries no candidate post-state or effects; it remains SHADOW, unmounted, and without proof or publication authority.
failure_modes: the proof boundary and runtime execute different debit or credit arithmetic
an accepted transfer omits the debit, mints recipient value, or changes aggregate asset atoms
insufficient source funds or recipient overflow produces a candidate post-state
insufficient funds loses stable precedence when recipient addition would also overflow
zero, excess, or self-transfer commands are admitted
zero, excess, duplicate, reordered, or over-capacity balance cells become canonical state
a wrong pre-state root, command hash, or authorization subject is accepted
unrelated accounts or assets change during one transfer
semantic command, state, movement, or conservation fields are absent from commitments
empty, oversized, trailing, malformed, or noncanonical bytes decode
stable reject codes drift or fail nonzero lane-journal conversion
a new arithmetic, protocol, or test source escapes the exact governed source inventory

aaa.reason: Focused Rust cases arrange typed state and command fixtures, execute one constructor or transition, and assert exact outcomes; the Python launcher marks its Arrange, Act, and Assert phases explicitly.

reject_is_noop.reason: The pure function borrows immutable input and its rejected enum variant stores only one stable code, so no post-state, movement, effect row, receipt, mutation, or publication capability exists on a rejected path.

mutations.description: Actual no-debit mutant returned the original source balance; the focused protocol run failed seven tests with AssetConservationViolation before the source was restored.
Skip expected pre-root, command-hash, or authorization-subject matching.
Allow a 257th canonical balance cell or a transfer-created cell in a full state.
Omit a semantic command or pre-state field from command or receipt hashing.
Accept trailing, oversized, unknown-field, stale-version, or self-inconsistent encoded input.
Omit the shared core, protocol module, or Rust regression from the exact governed source inventory.

nonclaims: Expected root, command, and subject fields are ordinary data until a guest binds them to an authenticated occurrence, grant, nonce, profile, route, and release.
The bounded whole-state hash is not a complete durable sparse-Merkle lane-state proof and does not derive the global post-state root.
The account-movement row is not a reconciled global effect plan and carries no settlement capability.
Kani evidence covers only the shared arithmetic function under its explicit admitted-domain assumptions.
The 48-byte runtime account representation still needs an explicit adapter and migration mapping to the 32-byte global account identifier.
No RISC0 guest was added while the governed workspaces remain on 3.0.5 and the whole-economy plan requires exact 3.0.6.
No issue, burn, fee, nonce, migration, terminal lifecycle, release activation, route mount, API, UI, Tau, recovery, legacy writer, or ZenoLedger publication path is added.
No RC, production-readiness, full-layer formal-verification, or whole-economy settlement claim is promoted.
